mainEntity.name: How much does a Range Rover 4.4 TDV8 engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text:
A reconditioned or rebuilt Range Rover 4.4 TDV8 engine typically costs between £6,000 and £12,000 for the supply-only unit, depending on the level of rebuild and specialist documentation provided.
- Rebuilt units include upgraded oil cooler seals and cooling system components.
- Supply and fit packages are available through our premium specialist network.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of oil cooler failure in a Range Rover 4.4 TDV8?

acceptedAnswer.text:
Early detection is critical to preventing catastrophic damage to your Range Rover 4.4 TDV8 engine.
- Look for unexplained coolant loss, oil contamination (milky appearance), or coolant/oil mixing.
- Overheating warnings, white smoke from the exhaust, or a sweet smell from the engine bay are also strong indicators.

mainEntity.name: Is the Range Rover 4.4 TDV8 more reliable than the 3.6 TDV8?

acceptedAnswer.text:
Yes, the 4.4 TDV8 is significantly more reliable than the earlier 3.6 TDV8.
- The 3.6 TDV8 suffered from crankshaft fracture and timing chain tensioner failures, while the 4.4 TDV8 has no catastrophic bottom-end design flaw.
- The 4.4 TDV8 is considered one of the most durable diesel V8s in the Land Rover lineup when properly maintained.

mainEntity.name: How long does a Range Rover 4.4 TDV8 engine supply and fit take?

acceptedAnswer.text:
A straightforward supply and fit replacement for a Range Rover 4.4 TDV8 typically takes 4 to 6 days at a premium specialist workshop.
- This allows time for the engine to be delivered, mounted, and thoroughly calibrated and tested.
- The V8 configuration requires more labour hours (18-24 hrs) than inline engines.

mainEntity.name: Can I upgrade my Range Rover 3.6 TDV8 to a 4.4 TDV8 engine?

acceptedAnswer.text:
While both are diesel V8s, a direct swap is not straightforward.
- The 4.4 TDV8 requires different ECU mapping, wiring harnesses, and potentially upgraded cooling and transmission components.
- We strongly recommend sticking to a like-for-like 448DT replacement to ensure guaranteed compatibility, MOT compliance, and warranty coverage.

historyTimeline.h2: Range Rover 4.4 TDV8 - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The 4.4-litre TDV8 (448DT) represented a significant evolution in Land Rover's diesel V8 lineup, offering improved refinement and durability compared to the earlier 3.6-litre unit, and became the preferred diesel V8 choice for Range Rover and Range Rover Sport models.

milestones.description: 448DT (4367cc), 313hp, introduced in the Range Rover L322 facelift and Range Rover Sport L320, replacing the problematic 3.6 TDV8 with a more robust 4.4-litre Ford-sourced V8 diesel.
2021 - Continued use in Range Rover L405 and Range Rover Sport L494, proving to be one of the most reliable diesel V8s in the Land Rover lineup with no catastrophic bottom-end design flaws.

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every engine fitted to the Range Rover 4.4 TDV8 is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points.

commonProblems.h2: Range Rover 4.4 TDV8 Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Range Rover 4.4 TDV8 (448DT) is widely regarded as one of the most reliable diesel V8s in Land Rover's modern lineup. Unlike the earlier 3.6 TDV8 with its crankshaft fracture risk, the 4.4-litre unit has no catastrophic bottom-end design flaw. However, high-mileage examples can develop oil cooler leaks and cooling system issues. Rebuilt engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.group: Oil Cooler Leaks & Cooling System Issues
problems.h4: Oil Cooler Leaks & Cooling System Issues - Why the Range Rover 4.4 TDV8 448DT Requires Attention
problems.rootCause: Oil cooler seals located in the valley of the V8 can degrade over time, leading to oil/coolant mixing. Coolant crossover pipes can also develop leaks due to age and thermal cycling.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace oil cooler seals, coolant crossover pipes, and thermostat housing.
repairOptions.longevity: Cost-effective if caught early with no major contamination or overheating damage.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, upgraded components addressing the original failure point, 12-month warranty.
repairOptions.longevity: Required if severe oil/coolant contamination has caused bearing wear or if the engine has suffered overheating damage.

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical 2010-2021 Range Rover or Range Rover Sport with 4.4 TDV8 is valued between £12,000 and £55,000 [THIRD-PARTY], with later L405/L494 models commanding the highest premiums. At this value band, an £8,000-£12,000 rebuilt engine replacement represents a sound investment (typically 15-40% of vehicle value), making it financially viable to protect your premium asset.
problems.recommendation: The 4.4 TDV8 is a robust engine that rewards proper maintenance. If your Range Rover has a full service history and the oil cooler leak is caught early, a specialist repair is highly cost-effective. However, if there is evidence of severe contamination, bearing wear, or the engine has exceeded 150,000 miles with patchy maintenance, a full reconditioned replacement is the most reliable long-term solution for a premium Range Rover.
